extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.publisher: IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Independent, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University
extraction.citeAs: Yue, X., Ni, Y., Zhang, K., Zheng, T., Liu, R., Zhang, G., Stevens, S., Jiang, D., Ren, W., Sun, Y., Wei, C., Yu, B., Yuan, R., Sun, R., Yin, M., Zheng, B., Yang, Z., Liu, Y., Huang, W., Sun, H., Su, Y., & Chen, W. (2024). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The questions were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. The collection took three stages: deciding subjects based on visual input commonality, recruiting students to collect/create questions, and quality control.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning: 1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. 2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. 3) Problems were categorized into difficulty levels, and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (50+ university students) collected multimodal questions from textbooks/online resources or created new ones. They adhered to copyright, avoided sites prohibiting redistribution, and selected questions without immediately available answers to avoid data contamination. Detailed protocol includes guidelines on question types (multiple-choice, open-ended), image types, format (JSON), and quality control (secondary review, regular audits).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioning information is provided in a Version Change Log (e.g., V1 Nov 27, V2 Dec 18, V3 Dec 21, V4 June 13). A live-updating leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Monitoring progress towards Expert AGI, which may lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption if achieved.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.
